deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a sheet on hyperelliptic Abelian functions. The 'Naturphil' bundle label and the previous page, which is about ether physics, are unrelated to its content. The page works toward expressing theta-constants at half-periods, θ(Σa+m), algebraically through the branch points. That is the content of what is now called Thomae's formula. A crossed-out note at the lower right reads roughly 'Thomae … Heft'.

(0) Top sketch. The branch points are paired as a_{p+1}, b_{p+1}, a_1, b_1, …, a_3, b_3. Dashed curves join a_ν to b_ν, and an outer loop is drawn. This is the usual picture of the cuts and period paths on the two-sheeted surface y^2 = Π(x−a)Π(x−b).

(1) Normalised integrals of the first kind. Riemann writes
v_ν = ∫ C_ν √(Π^{p+1}(x−a)) dx / [(x−a_ν) √(Π^{p+1}(x−b))] (with an extra (x−a_0) in the denominator).
• This amounts to a Lagrange-type basis of holomorphic differentials, each singled out by one branch point a_ν.
• The constants contain factors such as 1/(a_ν−a_0) and √((a_ν−a_ν')/(a_ν−b_ν')), and −πi.
• The periods are B^μ_ν = ∫_{a_μ}^{b_μ} dv_ν, taken along the cuts a_μ→b_μ.
• The table v_1 + B^1_1, B^2_1, …, B^p_1, …, v_p + B^1_p, … lists the shifts of each v_ν around the p cycles.

(2) Normalisation by the inverse period matrix. Write 𝔑 = det(B^μ_ν). Then
u_1 = (πi/𝔑) Σ_ν v_ν ∂𝔑/∂B^1_ν, and generally u_μ = (πi/𝔑) Σ_ν v_ν ∂𝔑/∂B^μ_ν.
• This is Cramer's rule: the cofactor ∂𝔑/∂B^μ_ν divided by 𝔑 is the inverse matrix.
• The u_μ therefore have periods πi δ_{μν} across the a→b cycles.
• The other periods, a_{μ,ν} (written α_{1,μ} = −(πi/𝔑) Σ …), form the symmetric theta matrix.

(3) Diagrams. The two staircase figures show how the paths from a_ν to b_ν, b_{ν−1}, a_{ν+1}, … are arranged. The aim is to relate integrals between consecutive branch points, such as ∫_{b_{ν−1}}^{a_ν} and ∫_{a_ν}^{b_ν}, to half-periods. This is the standard representation of half-periods as Abel images of branch points; the next page carries out the same bookkeeping for a change of cut system.

(4) Quotient formula. With m the Riemann constant (characteristic) and u the Abel image of x,
√(Π(x−a)/Π(x−b)) = A · θ(u − Σa + m)/θ(u − Σb + m), roughly.
This is Riemann's representation of the algebraic function √(Π(x−a)/Π(x−b)) as a theta quotient; the transcription garbles it as 'ϑ(u)−Σ(a)'.

(5) Evaluate the quotient formula at x = a_{p+1} and at x = b_{p+1}:
(i) √(Π(a_{p+1}−a)/Π(a_{p+1}−b)) = A θ(Σ^{p+1}a+m)/θ(a_{p+1}+Σ^p b+m)
(ii) √(Π(b_{p+1}−a)/Π(b_{p+1}−b)) = A θ(b_{p+1}+Σa+m)/θ(Σ^{p+1}b+m)

He then sets A = ⁴√[Π(a_{p+1}−a)(b_{p+1}−a)/Π(a_{p+1}−b)(b_{p+1}−b)]. My reading: this is the product (i)·(ii), together with the claim that the product of the two theta quotients equals 1 (a symmetry between the characteristics). Dividing (i) by A gives
θ(Σ^{p+1}a+m)/θ(a_{p+1}+Σ^p b+m) = ⁴√[Π(a_{p+1}−a) Π^p(b_{p+1}−b) / (Π(a_{p+1}−b) Π^p(b_{p+1}−a))] · (factors Π(a−a')Π(b−b')/Π(a−b') …).

(6) Target. The aim, stated at the left, is θ(Σ^{p+1}a+m) = K ⁴√(…).
• Later it is written as √(λ_p 𝔞_p), with λ_p 𝔞_p = (−2πi)^p · (…) and a recursion λ_{p−1}𝔞_{p−1}.
• That is: θ^4 at a half-period = constant (built from the period determinant and powers of −2πi) × Π(a−a') Π(b−b') over branch points in the same class.
• This is exactly the structure of Thomae's formula θ[η]^4 = c · Π_{i<j∈U}(e_i−e_j) Π_{i<j∉U}(e_i−e_j).
• The constant K is apparently to be fixed by induction on p (λ_p from λ_{p−1}).
errors: At x = a_{p+1}, the radicand Π(x−a) contains the factor (x−a_{p+1}) and vanishes. The corresponding theta numerator also vanishes. So (i) is meaningful only with that factor removed, i.e. as a limit or derivative, and with the product read over a ≠ a_{p+1}. The page leaves this implicit; the later Π^p notation suggests Riemann meant products omitting the coincident factor.
A = ⁴√(product of the two radicands) requires θ(Σa+m)θ(b_{p+1}+Σa+m) = θ(a_{p+1}+Σb+m)θ(Σb+m), up to sign and eighth roots of unity. This step is not justified on the page.
Signs and roots of unity (eighth roots arising from the characteristics) are not tracked. The fourth-root expressions are only determined up to such factors.
The constant λ_p 𝔞_p = (−2πi)^p … is begun and struck out. The normalising constant is not completed on this page.

results.what: Normalisation of hyperelliptic integrals of the first kind via the inverse period matrix written with cofactors: u_μ = (πi/𝔑) Σ_ν v_ν ∂𝔑/∂B^μ_ν
results.modern_name: Normalised basis of holomorphic differentials (A-periods = πi·identity) and the Riemann period matrix

results.what: Algebraic function √(Π(x−a)/Π(x−b)) expressed as A θ(u−Σa+m)/θ(u−Σb+m)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures); published by Thomae (1866/1870), with Weierstrass/Rosenhain/Göpel antecedents in genus 2

results.what: Theta-constants at half-periods Σa+m expressed as K·⁴√(Π(a−a')Π(b−b')/…), derived by evaluating the quotient formula at branch points a_{p+1}, b_{p+1} and eliminating A
results.modern_name: Thomae's formula (theta-constants of hyperelliptic curves in terms of branch points)

deep.surprise_reason: Thomae was Riemann's student and acknowledged Riemann's lectures for the hyperelliptic theta-quotient formula, so Riemann's involvement is not unknown. Still, an autograph working toward Thomae's formula, with the evaluation-at-branch-points method and the inductive constant λ_p𝔞_p, is a notable unpublished detail. It sharpens the priority picture, especially given the apparent marginal reference to Thomae. It is not a fully completed result on this page.

checkable.asserts: Genus-1 Thomae: θ2^4/θ3^4 = k^2 = cross-ratio of branch points (0,1,k^2,∞); should be 0
Genus-1 normalising constant: θ3^2 = 2K/π, i.e. the constant is a period (analogue of λ_p 𝔞_p involving the period determinant)

transcription_corrections: The quotient formula reads A θ(u−Σa+m)/θ(u−Σb+m) (Abel image u of x), not 'ϑ(u) − Σ(a)' with subtraction outside the theta.
'a_1 = (πi/𝔑)Σ v_ν ∂𝔑/∂B^1_ν' should be u_1 (the normalised integral), consistent with the later line 'u_1 = …'.
'ϑ(Σ^{p+1}a+m) = K ∜' (left margin): the fourth root is of a product of branch-point differences, which the transcription leaves blank.
The crossed-out text at the right margin near A = ⁴√… appears to read 'Thomae … Heft', a reference to Thomae's notes, not '[-…-]'.
In 'ϑ(Σ^{p+1}a+m) = √(λ_p 𝔞_p)', the symbol is a Fraktur 𝔞_p (a constant), distinct from the branch point a_p.
'α_{1,μ} = −(πi/𝔑) Σ_ν … ∂𝔑_ν/∂B^1_ν' denotes the second-kind periods (theta matrix entries) of u_1, not a new integral.
